subject: Northshore Renewal: alternate pricing path and commit options
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@northshorehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@northshorehealth.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — northshore usage growth and options

Hi Karthik,

Hope you had a good quarter. Our finance and ML platform teams have reviewed Q1 usage (attached) and we expect consumption to grow ~70% over the next 12 months as new agents roll out. Renewal is coming up in June — we need to align on a path that: reduces unit cost at scale, preserves predictable spend, and lets us do a short-term price hold while we complete an internal procurement cadence.

High-level asks:
- A firm 12-month price hold from renewal date while we ramp (we can commit to an initial capacity bucket and then scale).
- One-time onboarding credits for our sandbox and migration run (estimated $15k).
- Option to increase committed capacity mid-term with pre-negotiated uplift rates.

Can you propose an alternate path that balances Redwood’s unit economics with our need for predictability? I’ve attached our Q1 usage export for reference.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, ML Platform
Northshore Health
Attachments: northshore_usage_report_q1_2027.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@northshorehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — northshore usage growth and options

Hi Elena — thanks for the context and the usage export. Really glad to hear about the ramp.

Summary of what we can do as an alternate path:
- 6-month guarded price hold from renewal date on the currently quoted unit price, with an automatic review at month 6 tied to actual tpm (tokens per minute) and a pre-agreed floor price.
- $12,000 onboarding credit applied at first invoice to cover sandbox and migration runs.
- Structured mid-term increase: a two-tier uplift schedule where you can add +25% capacity at a reduced uplift (+8% vs list) or +50% at +14% vs list, both with 30-day notice.
- If you sign up for a 12-month committed minimum (50% of projected Q2 run-rate), we can extend the price hold to 9 months and increase onboarding credit to $15k.

I’ve attached a pricing grid that maps commit sizes to effective unit prices. Would appreciate any guidance from procurement on which of these options best maps to your approval gates.

If helpful, happy to hop on a 30-min call Thursday to walk the grid with Laura (CC’d) and Marcus on our side.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_pricing_grid_q2_2027.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Northshore — proposed concession ladder and margin impact

Folks — forwarding Elena’s asks and my initial offer. Key points to validate:

1) Price hold length vs commit size:
   - 6-month hold (no commit) — modest risk; requires closer monitoring of peak sequences.
   - 9-month hold if they sign 12-month min at 50% projected Q2 — better economics.

2) Onboarding credit: $12k baseline vs $15k if term/commit added. Margin impact roughly: $3k incremental credit reduces expected NRR by ~0.6% over the year.

3) Mid-term uplift tiers — need Marcus to confirm we can guarantee the +8%/+14% uplift on the Dedicated pools (GPU availability constraints).

Request: Marcus, can you confirm capacity headroom for a +50% bump with 30-day notice in the us-west region? Monica, if procurement pushes for a 12-month price hold without commit, what minimum concession level for credits/SLAs would you want?

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@northshorehealth.com>

Cc: Northshore Procurement <procurement@northshorehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — northshore usage growth and options

Hi Karthik and team — thanks for the quick proposal. A few clarifications from procurement and finance: 

- Procurement is comfortable with a firm 9-month price hold only if we can secure the 12-month committed minimum at 50% of projected Q2 run-rate and a written clause for a single mid-term uplift at the +25% tier.
- Finance would prefer the onboarding credit to be the full $15k without additional term conditions; they see the migration cost as a one-time implementation expense.
- We need the mid-term uplift rates to be fixed in the contract (no later re-pricing) and a clearly defined trigger for the ramp (API token thresholds + 30-day notice).

If you can send a redline-ready term sheet reflecting: 9-month hold, 12-month 50% commit, $15k onboarding credit, and fixed uplift schedule, we can fast-track to procurement signature.

Best,
Elena
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@northshorehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Apr 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — northshore usage growth and options

Elena — great, thanks. Laura and Marcus have confirmed we can support a 9-month price hold if Northshore signs the 12-month 50% commit. We’ll lock the mid-term uplift at the +25% tier (8% uplift) with the 30-day notice trigger and include a precise API token threshold in the contract schedule.

We can also accept the $15k onboarding credit applied at first invoice. I’ll get a redline-ready term sheet from Legal by EOD tomorrow and share the DocuSign link.

Next steps:
- I’ll circulate the redline-friendly term sheet and the HubSpot deal record.
- Please confirm the contact in procurement who will sign.

Appreciate the collaboration — happy to run a short exec summary for renewals if procurement wants it for their packet.

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
